summary: Iter 47 — Special Order FASE 3 (auto PR/PO on lock-price, warehouse default, in_production, convert-to-SO with locked price, printing category fallback, submit endpoint). Backend pytest 17/18 passed. Frontend verified for baseline sord_dab2dcbc0de9 detail, draft OD 'Ajukan persetujuan' → Menunggu Persetujuan, and CreateSpecialOrderForm printing category selects. ONE REAL BUG in auto_procure: PO uses the FIRST active supplier contract regardless of product_id — new OD winning contract price is ignored.

critical.issue: auto_procure picks a stale supplier contract (KSC/SCT-00025 at Rp 38.000 without product_id) instead of the newly-created winner contract (e.g. KSC/SCT-00027 at Rp 40.000). Reproduced on brand-new OD sord_48d82bff6182 (SORD-260919-0015): decide price=40000 → pricing.cost_price=40000, pricing.contract_number='KSC/SCT-00027' but linked PO items[0].price=38000, contract_number='KSC/SCT-00025'. SO conversion is unaffected (uses pricing.final_unit_price=50000). BUT the physical procurement PO is under-priced vs. winning supplier's promised contract — supplier will refuse or invoice differs.

backend_verified: GET /api/special-orders/sord_dab2dcbc0de9 → status in_production, linked_pr_number PR-00010, linked_po_number KSC/PO-00016, chain.po[0].supplier_name 'Solo Weave', chain.so.order_number KSC/SO-00016.

Full new OD flow (SORD-260919-0015, sord_48d82bff6182): create(labdip)+submit_for_approval → pending_approval → manager approve → confirmed + sample_ids[0] populated. send({supplier_ids:['sup_343fce6af69e'], type_codes:['labdip']}) → attach PNG → submit{note, measurements delta_e/wash/rub} → assess{acc, 90} → decide by admin (creator was manager) with price=40000, approve_spec, product_sku=OD-F3-<rnd> → decision.product_id populated. customer-decision acc → chain.phase=pricing. GET /api/warehouses returned 200. lock-price {margin_pct:25, warehouse_id, auto_po:true} → pricing.procurement.po_number set, no procurement_error, OD.status=in_production, chain.po[0].supplier_name='Solo Weave', chain.po[0].expected_delivery_date='2026-12-20'. GET PO → items[0].product_id=decision.product_id, quantity=120, warehouse_id=wh (BUT unit_price=38000, expected 40000 — see critical bug). Product lifecycle='produksi', exclusive_customer_id=cust_textile_medan. unlock-price by admin → 400 (PR/PO/SO already generated). convert-to-so → sales_order.items[0].product_id=decision.product_id, price=50000 (=40000*1.25), special_order_price=true, margin_pct=25; OD.linked_sales_order_id populated. Re-convert-to-so → 400 (idempotent).

action_items: HIGH — Fix backend/services/special_order_phase2.py::auto_procure so PO uses the WINNING sample contract price (pricing.cost_price / pricing.contract_number). Currently pr_svc.convert_to_po(pr_id, supplier_id, ...) delegates contract lookup to sourcing which picks the first active supplier contract regardless of product_id/sample_ref. Options: (a) pass the explicit contract_id to convert_to_po; (b) prefer contracts whose product_id matches or whose sample_ref matches pricing.sample_number; (c) after conversion, override items[].price back to pricing.cost_price and set contract_id/contract_number/price_source='special_order'.
OPTIONAL — auto_procure creates PR with est_price=pricing.cost_price but convert_to_po later overrides — remove misleading est_price signal or feed it into contract selection.
critical_code_review_comments: special_order_phase2.py::auto_procure — passes supplier_id but NOT contract_id when calling pr_svc.convert_to_po. That routine's sourcing prefers the first matching active contract; when a supplier has multiple contracts (labdip generic + product-specific), the LABDIP-generic contract (no product_id) is picked. Should scope by product_id or explicitly pass the winner contract_id from pricing.

special_order_phase2.py::lock_price — `pricing.contract_number` is stored on OD but never re-verified during PO creation, so the OD's audit trail claims one contract while the PO uses a different one. Consider asserting equality post-PO or embedding contract_id on OD.pricing.
special_orders.py::unlock_price — status_code inference `400 if user.role=='admin' else 403` still hides the ODError kind when non-admin errors. Recommend explicit role check first (as noted iter46).

special_orders.py::convert_to_so — SO uses pricing.final_unit_price correctly via sales_orders.py L190-198 — verified 50000=40000*1.25. This confirms cost_price is correct in pricing; only the physical PO price is wrong.

rca of the issue: auto_procure calls pr_svc.convert_to_po(pr_id, supplier_id, ...) without an explicit contract_id. Downstream contract-sourcing (services/pricing/sourcing.py) selects the first active contract for that supplier — when the supplier has a legacy/generic contract with empty product_id (as Solo Weave does via KSC/SCT-00025 from an earlier labdip sample), it wins over the newer product-specific contract created at /decide. Reproduction steps documented in test_09_verify_po. Fix: force convert_to_po to use pricing.contract_number/id or override PO item price post-conversion to pricing.cost_price.
